contentStandardDescription: Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicatorDescription: Observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Plant specimens; pictures of trees/flowers; garden visit; hand lens; Ecosystem chart; community walk; pictures of different habitats
keywords: observe, describe, different, kinds, things, environment
rpk: Learners have seen various plants, animals, and non-living objects in their school and home environment.
starter: Greet learners warmly and sing a happy Mother-Tongue science rhyme.
Show a real-world specimen (like a green plant, or a clean stone) and ask: 'What do you see? Touch it and describe it.'
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin exploring 1. living and non-living things.'
Write the key word 'observe' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher leads a safe walk into the schoolyard or school garden. Teacher points to a living plant and a non-living stone, describing how they look and feel.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Discovery - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups with hand lenses to observe leaves, tree barks, soil, or ants. They describe their observations to their peers.
ACTIVITY 3 (Drawing & Sorting - 7 min): Pupils return to the classroom and draw 2 living things and 2 non-living things in their notebooks, coloring them.
ACTIVITY 4 (Discussion & Sharing - 3 min): Selected pupils show their drawings to the class and describe one feature. Teacher reinforces concepts using mother tongue where necessary.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on CYCLES.
assessment: Observation worksheet; teacher observation rubric

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that some events in our environment occur recurrently
indicatorDescription: Explain that some natural phenomena, such as day and night, occur repeatedly.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: explain that some natural phenomena, such as day and night, occur repeatedly.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Pictures of sun, moon, sky; weather chart; flashlight (for sun-moon demo); globe or ball
keywords: explain, natural, phenomena, day, night, occur, repeatedly
rpk: Learners experience day and night daily, and see rain, sun, wind, and clouds in their daily lives.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and mimic the sun rising (stretch up high) and rain falling (wiggle fingers down).
Ask a quick question: 'What is the main source of light when we walk outside in the morning?'
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We are starting our study of 1. earth science.'
Write today's key term: 'explain' on the board and pronounce it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates. E.g., for day and night, teacher explains that the sun provides light. E.g., for rain, teacher uses a sponge to show how clouds hold water.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Outdoor Observation - 5 min): Pupils go outside to observe the clouds, wind direction, or feel the sun's warmth. They record their findings using simple weather symbols.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils construct simple paper fans or draw weather symbols on cardboard, coloring them.
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Pupils hold up their drawings. Teacher asks: 'What do we do on a rainy day? What about a sunny day?' Pupils share their thoughts.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Oral Q&A; short-answer test (5 marks); drawing of day and night scenes

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicatorDescription: Identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Human body chart; mirrors; pictures of body parts; senses-station activity (objects to feel, hear, see, smell, taste); 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' song
keywords: identify, external, human, body, parts, appropriate, names, senses
rpk: Learners are aware of their own body, hands, eyes, nose, and mouth, and use them daily.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Sing the 'Five Senses Song' or 'This is My Body' with appropriate active movements.
Have pupils look at their hands and wiggle their fingers. Ask: 'What do our hands help us do?'
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we will learn about 1. the human body systems.'
Write the keyword 'identify' on the board and pronounce it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher points to their own external body parts (eyes, ears, nose, hands, chest) and states their appropriate names, describing their functions.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Peer Identification - 5 min): Pupils sit in pairs, look at each other, and identify body parts. They chant together: 'These are my eyes, these are my ears.'
ACTIVITY 3 (Senses Activity - 7 min): Teacher sets up simple stations for sight, hearing, touch, and smell. Pupils rotate in pairs to guess objects, identifying the body part used.
ACTIVITY 4 (Active Game - 3 min): Play 'Simon Says touch your knees, shoulders, toes, chest.' Teacher monitors to ensure all pupils can correctly identify their body parts.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Practical body parts labeling; class exercise (classification table); Simon Says game

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources
indicatorDescription: Understand energy and give examples of its uses.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: understand energy and give examples of its uses.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation
resources: Torch; candle; battery; drum/bell; pictures of energy sources (sun, food, fuel); toy car
keywords: understand, energy, give, examples, uses, light, sound, heat, electricity
rpk: Learners have played with moving toys, felt heat, and seen lights and electrical appliances at home.
starter: Greet learners. Rub hands together quickly until they feel warm. Ask: 'What do you feel? Where did the warmth come from?'
Demonstrate pushing a toy block or ball. Ask: 'Why did it move?'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we will begin learning about 1. sources and forms of energy.'
Write the keyword 'understand' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates a concept. E.g., for forces, teacher pushes a chair and pulls a drawer. E.g., for simple machines, shows how a ramp (inclined plane) makes work easier.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils test pushing and pulling various classroom objects (books, bottles, blocks, pencil cases) and state whether it was a push or a pull.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Active Experiment - 7 min): In small groups, pupils explore simple sources of energy (feeling warm sunlight, safely touching warm objects, observing a glowing torch/circuit).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing - 3 min): Pupils explain their findings: 'A push moves things away, a pull brings things closer.' Teacher writes these summaries on the board.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Practical demonstration; class exercise (identifying energy uses in the classroom)

contentStandardDescription: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicatorDescription: Explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
competencies: Personal Development & Leadership; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Soap; sponge; towel; bucket; basin; tippy-tap; water; hygiene poster showing bathing steps; doll/toy for bathing roleplay
keywords: explain, need, bathing, cleanliness, health, germs, how, done, soap
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Show a hygiene tool (e.g., a real soap bar or a clean toothbrush) and ask: 'Who used this today?'
Sing a joyful song about personal cleanliness and health with actions.
NEW TODAY: Introduce the lesson: 'Today we will learn about 1. personal hygiene and sanitation.'
Write the keyword 'explain' on the board and pronounce it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates. E.g., for handwashing, models the 6 steps with real soap and running water from a tippy-tap. E.g., for teeth, models correct brushing steps on a model.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Active Practice - 5 min): Pupils take turns at the washing station to practice the 6 standard handwashing steps, or practice brushing techniques in pairs.
ACTIVITY 3 (Creative Group Poster - 7 min): In small groups, pupils color a hygiene poster representing bathing, handwashing, or waste disposal, and label key items using crayons.
ACTIVITY 4 (Hygiene Demonstration - 3 min): A pupil is selected to demonstrate correct handwashing or teeth-cleaning steps to the class. Teacher prompts and class praises.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Oral Q&A; bathing roleplay/demonstration; short-answer test

contentStandardDescription: Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicatorDescription: Observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Plant specimens; pictures of trees/flowers; garden visit; hand lens; Ecosystem chart; community walk; pictures of different habitats
keywords: observe, describe, different, kinds, things, environment
rpk: Learners have seen various plants, animals, and non-living objects in their school and home environment.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Begin with a local call-and-response song about the natural world around us.
Play a 3-minute game of 'I Spy' where pupils spot a living or non-living thing in the classroom.
Review key words from previous sessions: observe, describe, different.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we are going to review and show what we know about 1. living and non-living things.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Interactive Review - 5 min): Teacher displays living and non-living objects (or cards). Pupils call out 'Living!' or 'Non-living!' in unison and explain why.
ACTIVITY 2 (Pair sorting - 5 min): In pairs, pupils sort physical specimens (leaves, twigs, plastic pens, stones) on their desks. Teacher checks and guides.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Challenge - 7 min): Groups are given cards of natural and man-made materials. They play a race game to sort them into correct trays.
ACTIVITY 4 (Consolidation - 3 min): Teacher clarifies any misconceptions, reviews the key term 'observe', and praises excellent team effort.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Observation worksheet; teacher observation rubric

starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.

Recall how energy and forces make objects move or make work easier.

ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.

contentStandardDescription: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicatorDescription: Explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
competencies: Personal Development & Leadership; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Soap; sponge; towel; bucket; basin; tippy-tap; water; hygiene poster showing bathing steps; doll/toy for bathing roleplay
keywords: explain, need, bathing, cleanliness, health, germs, how, done, soap
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners. Sing an active hygiene song like 'This is the way we wash our hands/brush our teeth.'
Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 1. personal hygiene and sanitation.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.
ACTIVITY 2 (Roleplay & Practice - 5 min): In small groups, pupils practice the 6-step handwashing technique using a real bar of soap and clean basins (or dry run) or roleplay brushing teeth.
ACTIVITY 3 (Surroundings Cleanup - 7 min): Pupils play a cleanup game, picking up safe trash (paper, plastic) in the classroom/schoolyard and sorting it into correct organic/inorganic bins.
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'

Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).

rpk: Learners experience day and night daily, and see rain, sun, wind, and clouds in their daily lives.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and mimic the sun rising (stretch up high) and rain falling (wiggle fingers down).
Ask a quick question: 'What is the main source of light when we walk outside in the morning?'
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We are starting our study of 1. earth science.'
Write today's key term: 'observe' on the board and pronounce it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates. E.g., for day and night, teacher explains that the sun provides light. E.g., for rain, teacher uses a sponge to show how clouds hold water.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils construct simple paper fans or draw weather symbols on cardboard, coloring them.
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Pupils hold up their drawings. Teacher asks: 'What do we do on a rainy day? What about a sunny day?' Pupils share their thoughts.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Oral Q&A; class discussion; drawing the puddle drying up

performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: know examples of common electronic devices and their uses.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Mobile phone; tablet; calculator; television remote; dry cells; wires; simple LED bulb
keywords: know, examples, common, electronic, devices, uses, technology, entertainment
rpk: Learners have played with moving toys, felt heat, and seen lights and electrical appliances at home.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.
Have pupils stand up, push their chairs in, and then pull them out. Ask: 'What forces did we just use?'
Recall how energy and forces make objects move or make work easier.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will review and consolidate our understanding of 2. electricity and electronics.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Forces/Energy Recap - 5 min): Teacher displays a toy machine, ramp, or electronic device. Pupils call out what force or energy it uses or how it helps us.
ACTIVITY 2 (Hands-on Ramps/Cars - 5 min): In small groups, pupils roll toy cars on smooth and rough surfaces to observe movement. They describe which surface has less resistance.
ACTIVITY 3 (Practical Investigation - 7 min): Pupils use simple materials (balloons, cardboard, rubber bands) to explore pushes, pulls, and energy. They draw their findings in their notebooks.
ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical demonstration (using a simple device); class discussion; device-use log

contentStandardDescription: Understand waste management and practice waste separation
indicatorDescription: Identify and describe different types of waste in the school and home environment.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: identify and describe different types of waste in the school and home environment.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Trash bin; rubbish bins (labelled: organic, plastic, paper); schoolyard walk; garbage samples (safe/clean paper, plastic bottles, orange peels, cans)
keywords: identify, describe, types, waste, rubbish, organic, inorganic, plastic, school, home
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Show a hygiene tool (e.g., a real soap bar or a clean toothbrush) and ask: 'Who used this today?'
Sing a joyful song about personal cleanliness and health with actions.
NEW TODAY: Introduce the lesson: 'Today we will learn about 3. waste management.'
Write the keyword 'identify' on the board and pronounce it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates. E.g., for handwashing, models the 6 steps with real soap and running water from a tippy-tap. E.g., for teeth, models correct brushing steps on a model.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Active Practice - 5 min): Pupils take turns at the washing station to practice the 6 standard handwashing steps, or practice brushing techniques in pairs.
ACTIVITY 3 (Creative Group Poster - 7 min): In small groups, pupils color a hygiene poster representing bathing, handwashing, or waste disposal, and label key items using crayons.
ACTIVITY 4 (Hygiene Demonstration - 3 min): A pupil is selected to demonstrate correct handwashing or teeth-cleaning steps to the class. Teacher prompts and class praises.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Waste sorting task; class discussion on organic and inorganic waste; trash walk worksheet

contentStandardDescription: Recognise materials as important resources for providing human needs
indicatorDescription: Describe and group materials by their appearance (shape, size, colour, texture).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: describe and group materials by their appearance (shape, size, colour, texture).
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Samples of common materials (wood, metal, plastic, fabric); sorting trays; hand lenses; textured fabric pieces
keywords: describe, group, materials, appearance, shape, size, colour, texture
rpk: Learners have seen various plants, animals, and non-living objects in their school and home environment.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Begin with a local call-and-response song about the natural world around us.
Play a 3-minute game of 'I Spy' where pupils spot a living or non-living thing in the classroom.
Review key words from previous sessions: describe, group, materials.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we are going to review and show what we know about 2. materials.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Interactive Review - 5 min): Teacher displays living and non-living objects (or cards). Pupils call out 'Living!' or 'Non-living!' in unison and explain why.
ACTIVITY 2 (Pair sorting - 5 min): In pairs, pupils sort physical specimens (leaves, twigs, plastic pens, stones) on their desks. Teacher checks and guides.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Challenge - 7 min): Groups are given cards of natural and man-made materials. They play a race game to sort them into correct trays.
ACTIVITY 4 (Consolidation - 3 min): Teacher clarifies any misconceptions, reviews the key term 'describe', and praises excellent team effort.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical sorting task; class exercise; matching worksheet

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of air and water in our environment
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate the existence of air in the environment.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: demonstrate the existence of air in the environment.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Balloons; plastic cups; water basins; paper windmills/fans; plastic bags; straws
keywords: demonstrate, existence, air, environment, wind, blow, space
rpk: Learners experience day and night daily, and see rain, sun, wind, and clouds in their daily lives.
starter: Greet learners. Recite a fun weather poem together: 'Sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, we love all weather!' with physical gestures.
Ask: 'What changes did you see in the sky on your way to school today?'
Review yesterday's lesson: the recurring natural events in our immediate environment.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice and show what we have learned about 1. earth science.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Weather/Day-Night Recap - 5 min): Teacher displays weather symbols on the board. Pupils match them to words (sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy) and discuss how they change.
ACTIVITY 2 (Interactive Demonstration - 5 min): Teacher uses a globe/ball and flashlight to demonstrate the repeating day and night cycle. Pupils take turns holding the light.
ACTIVITY 3 (Worksheet / Matching - 7 min): Pupils complete a matching worksheet, matching day/night to activities (e.g., sleeping at night, playing during the day) or matching weather to clothing.
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher corrects common errors on the worksheets and summarizes the natural cycle of 1. earth science.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical demonstration; teacher observation; balloon blowing challenge

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicatorDescription: Identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Human body chart; mirrors; pictures of body parts; senses-station activity (objects to feel, hear, see, smell, taste); 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' song
keywords: identify, external, human, body, parts, appropriate, names, senses
rpk: Learners are aware of their own body, hands, eyes, nose, and mouth, and use them daily.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' together with rapid physical actions.
Play 'Simon Says' to identify and touch external body parts quickly.
Recall why we need our body parts to work interdependently to play and learn.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice identifying and describing our 1. the human body systems.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Body Parts Game - 5 min): Play an accelerated game of 'Simon Says' or point to body parts to test speed and accuracy. Pupils clap for correct answers.

ACTIVITY 2 (Senses Exploration - 5 min): In small groups, pupils explore different sense objects (rough stone, smelling flower, hearing bell, tasting safely). They identify which body part is responsible.
ACTIVITY 3 (Human Body Chart - 7 min): In small groups, pupils paste labels (eyes, ears, hand, chest, shoulders, leg) onto a large blank outline of a human body.
ACTIVITY 4 (Feedback & Review - 3 min): Each group displays their body chart. Teacher provides positive feedback and reinforces vocabulary: identify, external, human.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical body parts labeling; class exercise (classification table); Simon Says game

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of forces and their effects on objects
indicatorDescription: Understand that movement is caused by applied forces (push or pull).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: understand that movement is caused by applied forces (push or pull).

resources: Toy cars; ramps; balls; blocks; rubber bands; balloons; chairs to push/pull

starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.

Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 3. waste management.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.

ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.

Review key words from previous sessions: identify, classify, materials.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we are going to review and show what we know about 2. materials.'

ACTIVITY 4 (Consolidation - 3 min): Teacher clarifies any misconceptions, reviews the key term 'identify', and praises excellent team effort.
